1xbet-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
1xbet-update.description: Isolated 1xBet soccer odds, pushed on change. 1xBet soccer is not part of odds-update; it has its own REST endpoint and this event.

4casters-v2-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
4casters-v2-update.description: 4casters Source API (v2) event deltas from a peer-to-peer betting exchange. Each entry is a whole event carrying its full order book: every resting offer with its own price and the size still available on it (sumUntaken), plus matched volume. Alternate spreads and totals appear as keyed rungs, and player props are separate leagues. Odds are American and may carry a half point.

odds-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
odds-update.description: Consensus odds for the sports and books in your subscription. After a subscribe the first frames are a snapshot of that shape; later frames carry only the games that changed, so merge by event id. A connection that never subscribes receives the default (all sports, all books) after a short grace. Subscriptions belong to one connection: send yours again after every reconnect.

pinnacle-realtime.access: WebSocket access plus MVP or above
pinnacle-realtime.description: Pinnacle real-time odds, sent to eligible connections for the sports in your subscription (all sports if you never subscribe; the books filter does not apply). Each frame carries one sport and at least one event: {timestamp, <sport>: [events], delta: true, resync?, stream?, removed?}. Events have the same fields as the data of GET /api/v1/{sport}/realtime, including status, isLive, phase when known, lastUpdate, seenAt and freshness; that endpoint's notes describe them. Frames are partial: merge each event into your board by event id, replacing the whole event, then delete the ids in removed[<sport>]. resync: true marks a frame from the periodic resend, which also carries events that have not changed. When present, stream is {sport, epoch, seq, checkpoint?}: seq goes up by 1 per frame for that sport within one epoch. Ignore a frame whose seq is at or below the last one you applied (a duplicate). A skipped seq, a new epoch, or a frame without stream after frames that had one means you must load the board again; keep your current board until the new one is ready. To load a board, on every connect or reconnect and after any of those: buffer the sport's frames from both pinnacle-realtime and pinnacle-realtime-sync, wait up to 25 seconds for one with stream.checkpoint set (load at once if the sport's frames carry no stream), then call GET /api/v1/{sport}/realtime and read its meta.stream. If meta.stream is null, replace your board with data, merge every frame with no seq filter, and load again after 10, 20, 40 seconds and so on, up to every 5 minutes; replacing the board is also what drops ended events while frames carry no removed. If its epoch differs from the checkpoint's, or its seq is lower than the checkpoint's, load again at the next checkpoint. Otherwise replace your board with data, discard buffered frames with a seq at or below meta.stream.seq, and apply the rest in order. Each load counts against your request quota. Stream positions and removals for a sport with no events to send arrive on pinnacle-realtime-sync. In soccer women's and youth leagues, team names carry a Women or Unn suffix taken from the league, as on the matching REST endpoint.

pinnacle-realtime-sync.access: WebSocket access plus MVP or above
pinnacle-realtime-sync.description: Companion of pinnacle-realtime, sent on the same connections and for the same sports: a stream position or removals for a sport that has no events to send, as {timestamp, sport, stream?, removed?}. Track stream and delete removed ids exactly as on pinnacle-realtime; it never carries events.

pinnacle-v2-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
pinnacle-v2-update.description: Pinnacle Source API (v2) per-matchup deltas: changed matchupIds plus the league hash, with a 30 second heartbeat per league (heartbeat: true) whose matchupIds is the full league membership rather than a change set. The hash equals the REST etag (without quotes) whenever that response is not partial, so a hash you already hold needs no refetch; otherwise refetch with If-None-Match, and a 304 on /api/v2 does not count toward the monthly quota. A delta or a heartbeat may also carry removedMatchupIds: matchup ids the league dropped, which you delete. That list is not exhaustive and an id can reappear later in matchupIds, so heartbeat membership and the REST board stay authoritative. When a league empties, its final heartbeat can carry an empty matchupIds; after that the league sends nothing until it has matchups again.

player-props-update.access: WebSocket access plus Rookie or above
player-props-update.description: Pinnacle player props, streamed on change. Subscribe with the subscribe-props event; the server acknowledges with props-subscribed.

polymarket-v2-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
polymarket-v2-update.description: Polymarket CLOB deltas: raw market objects plus price and orderbook changes for game lines and player props. League keys are Polymarket tag slugs from the /leagues index.

prophetx-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
prophetx-update.description: ProphetX sports exchange odds and liquidity deltas, pushed on change.

ps3838-realtime.access: WebSocket access plus MVP or above
ps3838-realtime.description: PS3838 real-time odds, sent to eligible connections for the sports in your subscription (all sports if you never subscribe; the books filter does not apply). Each frame carries one sport, and a frame can be several MB, so allow a client message size of at least 32 MB. In soccer women's and youth leagues, team names carry a Women or Unn suffix taken from the league, as on the matching REST endpoint.

server-heartbeat.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
server-heartbeat.description: A small {seq, ts} message every 10 seconds on every connection, independent of odds traffic, so silence is detectable. seq is counted by the server, not per connection: it goes up by 1 every 10 seconds, and after a reconnect it can jump ahead or start again from 1. Compare it only within one connection, where a gap means messages were missed.

server-notice.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
server-notice.description: Why the server closed your previous connection, sent once on the next connect: {code, message, at, socketId, details, hint}. Codes: BACKLOG_CAP, AGGREGATE_SHED, GHOST, SLOT_EVICTED, CLIENT_FRAME_LIMIT, SERVER_RESTART. SERVER_RESTART is sent to open connections just before a restart instead; reconnect after a short delay and send your subscription again.

thunderpick-v2-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
thunderpick-v2-update.description: Thunderpick Source API (v2) change notification per sport. Carries sport, count, hash and timestamp only; refetch the REST snapshot on receipt.

tippmixpro-v2-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
tippmixpro-v2-update.description: TippmixPro Source API (v2) market deltas from Hungary's state sportsbook (EveryMatrix platform), pushed as they happen. Each entry is one market with its outcomes and prices, plus one {matchId}-event entry per event carrying the match record and live score info. Odds are decimal. Multi-league sports need a league filter.

valorant-realtime.access: WebSocket access plus MVP or above
valorant-realtime.description: Pinnacle valorant realtime in the Pinnacle wire format (matchups, markets, prices).

versus-v2-update.access: WebSocket access: Hall of Fame, or any paid tier with the WebSocket add-on
versus-v2-update.description: versus.es Source API (v2) per-market deltas at poll cadence. Every sport is multi-league, so a league filter is required.
